title: answer --root WORKTREE commits the item file it changes on the worker's branch, so the orchestrator makes no hand git commit there
goal: Retrospective of SP-tm4wlsve: the orchestrator records an operator answer to a gate that exists only on a worker's branch with backlog.py --root WORKTREE answer, then a hand git -C WORKTREE commit of the item file. One such commit was refused by a permission rule (its message named GitHub and push), and land, started beside it, stopped at step branch on the uncommitted item file (ops SP-tm4wlsve land.end exit=1 for ST-t2j24bhx). answer --root WORKTREE commits the item file alone on the worker's branch with a fixed subject and KB-Work, as claim --commit does, and the kb-sprint skill's run step 4.1 names that form; a test answers a gate in a planted worktree and finds one new commit holding only the item file.
notes: Merged from ST-62ixsksb “A review's gate confirms are committed by the tool, so the orchestrator writes no KB-Work list by hand” at the 2026-10-12 draft triage: Premise holds: answer --record commits only for --answer, and bl_items.py:290 rejects --confirm with --record. Same hand-commit-refused-by-hook failure as ST-dq2klrkr; the carrier should also make the confirm path commit with a KB-Work line naming the items, comma-separated. Its goal: backlog.py answer --confirm (or a review command) commits the item files it changes with a KB-Work line naming exactly those items, as claim --commit and start --commit do; at SP-j2jn5ue4 the orchestrator's hand commit of four confirms was refused by the commit-msg hook twice (it named the review story, then space-separated ids) before the comma-separated list passed. Its checks: {"run": ["python3", "_tools/tests.py", "-k", "answer_confirm_commit"]}
